- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-package/vitest.config.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **14** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e246f06119e9c967d5e4ef3e56e74b6312ce2525` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `eac82e1b6bfd79361bd0afda1543f6091e25805f` — the merge of head `bb3838c8153b74cf54ebdb33c1b0665376851190` into base `e246f06119e9c967d5e4ef3e56e74b6312ce2525`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin eac82e1b6bfd79361bd0afda1543f6091e25805f && git checkout eac82e1b6bfd79361bd0afda1543f6091e25805f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e246f06119e9c967d5e4ef3e56e74b6312ce2525 bb3838c8153b74cf54ebdb33c1b0665376851190 && git checkout -B drift-repro e246f06119e9c967d5e4ef3e56e74b6312ce2525 && git merge --no-ff bb3838c8153b74cf54ebdb33c1b0665376851190

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e246f06119e9c967d5e4ef3e56e74b6312ce2525
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e246f06119e9c967d5e4ef3e56e74b6312ce2525` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Head-sha: `f1443d9bca310525ec1b6add5d6ffd28791aae2a`

Read at 2026-10-16T20:33Z, against the head named above. Inputs: card #23974's body and all four comments (`6219354007`, `6221631934`, `6222032665`, `6223102830`); this PR's body, its 12-file list and its one comment; the net diff `fd9664ff..f1443d9bca` (+734/-18, the same 12 files); and the 41 check-runs on the head, read last. Code was read with `git show` / `git grep` at the head. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

**Door 1: `sys_packages` boot hydration** (`packages/services/service-package/src/index.ts`)
- **Conversion before the judge: right.** `:693-695` binds the engine's own `convertPackageBodyForward`. `:738` hands `convertForward(rec.manifest)` to `registry.installPackage`. The entry point itself (`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts:7826`) is not in the diff.
- **A refusal is reported by name, and hydration goes on: right.** At `:737-748`, a record the registry refuses is logged at `error`, naming `'${id}'`, carrying the refusal's message, with the refusal attached as the second argument. The line states the consequence (absent from the registry while its row remains) and the fix (install a corrected build or uninstall, then restart), so it meets the degradation-level rule. The loop continues.
- **`isSeamUnreadable` WARN: unchanged.** `:755-775` is outside the diff.
- **`Hydrated N package(s)`: right.** `hydrated++` (`:739`) runs only after `installPackage` returns. Records the D1 handshake refuses (`continue`, `:720`), records already registered (`:703`) and records the registry refuses are all excluded.
- **Range-less, code-built manifest: right.** `convertPackageBodyForward` returns the body by reference when `resolveDeclaredRange` is null (`engine.ts:7828`). The registry judges the identical object. Only the reporting changed: before, the first refusal aborted the loop to a `debug` line; now it is an `error` and the loop continues.
- **No second judge, no silent skip: right.** The diff touches nothing under `packages/objectql/**`, `packages/metadata-core/**` or `packages/spec/**`.
- Cosmetic: if the converter itself threw, the `:742` sentence would blame the registry. The converter is documented as never throwing (`packages/metadata-core/src/artifact-forward-conversion.ts:486`), so this is not a defect.

**Door 2: `protocol.installPackage` stays strict** (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts:31393-31405`, a comment; the code is unchanged)
- **The dev's evidence is true at this head.**
  - **The HTTP door.** `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts:1353` refuses any body that `PackageInstallBodySchema` rejects, before the primitive is called (`:1396`). `ManifestSchema` (`packages/spec/src/kernel/manifest.zod.ts:457`) is a `strictObject` with no `pages` key, and its `objects` and `datasources` are glob-string arrays. So no body carrying a metadata collection reaches the primitive over HTTP. The no-protocol fallback (`:1408-1409`) is the same authoring door, and D1 is asserted there.
  - **`duplicatePackage`** (`:27480-27496`) spreads `srcPkg.manifest`, which is the registry's own record. Every converting door hands the registry the converted body (`engine.ts:7870`/`:7902`, door 1 `:738`, door 3 `:787`/`:1571`), so the copy is already converted.
  - **The unmanaged base** (`:27870`): consistent with the ADR-0131 D6 copy.
  - **AI Studio** lives in cloud and cannot be read here. Triage's reading (`6219354007`) puts it on this primitive, in-process, which makes it authoring by nature.
- **Is this the card's "authoring-side door that stays strict, recorded why"? Yes.** The card's first done-bullet and the claim's Responsibility line both allow it. That choice supersedes, for door 2, the card's second bullet ("passes door 1 and door 2 with the named warning"). It is recorded, not a defect.
- **The door-2 pin is real.** `hydration-convert-forward.test.ts:175-198` builds the real `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation` (aliased to metadata-protocol `src/`) over the real engine, registry and sqlite. It asserts `MisplacedDefaultPageError` (`INVALID_METADATA`, 422), no registry record, no `sys_packages` row and no conversion warning. A door 2 that converted would install the body and fail the first assertion.
  - Why the pin lives in service-package: `@objectstack/objectql` lists `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` in its `dependencies`, so metadata-protocol cannot import objectql. The cycle reason holds.
  - This leg was not ablated; A1-A4 cover doors 1 and 3.

**Door 3: the marketplace install** (`packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts`)
- **One conversion per load, the same object to every reader: right.**
  - Rehydrate: converted at `:782`, then `register` `:787`, the binder `:797`, the side effects `:802`, and the heal `:810`. The heal now takes `converted` (`:837-840`).
  - Install: converted at `:1565`, then `register` `:1571`, the binder `:1635`, and the side effects `:1642`.
  - The helper `:2790-2794` delegates to the engine's entry point. An engine without that door gets the body as before.
- **The ledger keeps the body as installed: right.** The install's entry (`:1594-1599`) carries the raw `manifest`. Rehydrate never rewrites `entry.manifest`; the heal's ledger write (`:868`) writes the raw entry. The conversion is copy-on-write. Pinned at test `:192` and `:204`.
- **No second warning.** `register` meets the entry point with an already-converted body, which yields no notices, and the engine also de-duplicates per (package, conversion) (`engine.ts:7841-7843`). The pins assert exactly one warning (`:190`, `:203`).
- **Raw `entry.manifest` readers left in the claimed region:** one, `checkProtocolCompat(entry.manifest)` at `:765`. That is the D1 handshake, and it must read the declared range before conversion; conversion never rewrites `engines`. Correct. The install's D1 (`:1363`) is the same.
- **The change only widens.** The binder now receives converted hooks: `hook-timeout-to-timeout-ms` renames a key, and `hook-body-crypto-hash-removed` strips a dead grant. No narrowing.

**The pins**
- **Both suites run over the real `SchemaRegistry`.**
  - service-package boots the real `ObjectKernel`, `ObjectQLPlugin`, `SqlDriver` (better-sqlite3 on disk) and `PackageServicePlugin`. One process publishes, a second hydrates. `:157` asserts the list order, so "the record after the refused one" really comes after it.
  - cloud-connection boots the real `ObjectKernel` and `ObjectQLPlugin`. Its `objectql` service is a bag that delegates to the real engine's converter and exposes the real `registry`, and its `manifest` service wraps the real one. The side readers are replaced by recorders, which is enough because the pin asserts which object they received.
- **Each converting door has a CONTROL:** door 1 at `:240-247`; door 3's install at `:212-224` and rehydrate at `:226-240`.
- **The ablation legs are the right mutations.** A1 removes door 1's conversion. A2 makes the per-record catch rethrow. A3 and A4 each revert one reader to the raw body, one per path. The `toBe(first.body)` loop covers every reader, so one ablated reader per path is enough. Door 2 has no leg; it is red by construction, but unmeasured.

**Premise correction: true.**
- The fixture `packages/objectql/src/__fixtures__/hotcrm-4.0.1-published-pages.artifact.json` declares `^17.7.0` on every manifest in it.
- `rangeAdmitsMajor` pins a caret's major (`packages/metadata-core/src/protocol-handshake.ts:265-268`), and `PROTOCOL_VERSION` is `18.0.0` (`packages/spec/src/kernel/protocol-version.ts:22`).
- So the body is `incompatible` at door 1 (`index.ts:713-720`), door 3 (`:765`, `:1363`) and door 2 (`:31386`).

**Is the restamp honest?**
- **For the conversion it is.** The conversion policy reads only the range's floor (`parseRangeFloor`, `artifact-forward-conversion.ts:516`). So `>=17.7.0` gets exactly the verdict and the chain that the published `^17.7.0` body would get if D1 admitted it: same floor, same pages.
- **It is not a range tooling stamps.** Scaffolds and the lint fix stamp `^N`, the current major (`packages/cli/src/commands/init.ts:849`, `lint.ts:583`).
- **The natural widening spelling is refused.** `^17.7.0 || ^18.0.0` is falsely refused by D1 (flag 1 below).
- **So on this runtime, the window at doors 1 and 3 is reached by:** a hand-written `>=` or hyphen range; an unparsed range (D1 admits it with a warning); and the realistic future case, a `^18` body built before a retirement inside major 18.

**What this means for the card's reach claim**
- The P0 suspect (one HotCRM-shaped row stops hydration) does not hold on v18 for HotCRM 4.0.1 as published. D1 refuses that row by name and `continue`s. That behaviour predates this PR and is now pinned (`:249-262`).
- The loop defect is real for any registry refusal of a row D1 admits, and this PR fixes it.
- The conversion half reaches only rows that declare a range, and `protocol.installPackage` stamps no `engines` (`:31361-31386`). Range-less tenant rows (AI Studio's, if they carry no range; unmeasured, in cloud) get loop survival and a named `error`, not conversion.
- The changeset's sentence ("a stored record whose range admits this runtime, built before a retirement") is accurate.

**Surface supplements outside the claim**
- **`service-package` devDependencies** (`driver-sql`, `metadata-protocol`, `objectql`): necessary, since the pin imports all three. Minimal. No cycle: none of the three depends on service-package.
- **`vitest.config.ts`:** four anchored aliases to `src/` (`core`, `objectql`, `metadata-protocol`, `driver-sql`). Necessary for `check:test-source-alias` and to keep one module instance. Minimal. The header edit ("two settings") is accurate.
- **`pnpm-lock.yaml`** (+9): exactly the three link entries. Minimal.
- **`scripts/cross-package-test-inputs.mjs`:** the cloud-connection glob and the new service-package entry, each the one fixture path. Necessary, because both tests read across packages through a recognised `resolve(HERE, …)` spelling. Minimal.
- **`turbo.json`:** the fixture added to `cloud-connection#test`'s inputs, and a new `service-package#test` task equal to the generic `test` task plus that one input. Necessary and minimal.
- **The gate edit (`f1443d9bca`):**
  - Some edit was needed. `scripts/cross-package-test-inputs.mjs` is a scanned, non-test file, and its new fixture line meets rule 3 (`__fixtures__` and `hotcrm` on one line), so the gate counted it as a loader.
  - This edit is not correct; see **R1**.
  - It is also undeclared: neither the PR body's "Wiring the pins needed" nor the dev report (taken at `fe7b944bb`) names it.

**The gate edit: a precision fix in intent, a weakening as written** (`scripts/check-position-name-fold-loaders.mjs`)
- **How the new rule works.** Before rule 3 is asked, `:160-166` deletes from the line every match of `OTHER_PACKAGE_FIXTURE_PATH`. A match is kept only when the RAW match string starts with `packages/metadata/src/__fixtures__/` or has a `..` segment.
- **Leak 1: a `.` segment.** A path through `packages/./metadata/src/__fixtures__/` or `packages/metadata/./src/__fixtures__/` resolves to the guarded directory. Rule 2 misses it, because the text never contains the literal `packages/metadata/src/__fixtures__`. It passes the raw `startsWith` test and has no `..` segment, so it is set aside.
- **Leak 2: a partial match.** `[\w.-]+` stops at the first glob or template character, so a match can end mid-path. Its glob-free prefix is deleted, and the remainder carries no `__fixtures__` to meet rule 3. This contradicts the docblock at `:155-157` ("A path that … carries a glob character is never set aside").
- **Together they let these spellings through.** Each red before this commit and passes at this head, traced by hand against the regex:
  - `` readFileSync(`packages/./metadata/src/__fixtures__/hotcrm-17.1-${kind}.artifact.json`) `` (Node resolves the `.` segment)
  - `glob('packages/./metadata/src/__fixtures__/hotcrm-*.artifact.json')`
  - `glob('packages/metadata/./src/__fixtures__/hotcrm-*.artifact.json')`

  Each one names or sweeps up `hotcrm-17.1-built-permissions.artifact.json`, the artifact whose non-test load this gate exists to red, because that load grants `sales_rep` and `sales_manager` by name.
- **Not leaks:**
  - a `..` segment (kept);
  - backslash or mixed separators (the regex needs `/`, and a `..` before a backslash is kept);
  - a glob in the package segment, or directly after `__fixtures__/` (no match);
  - a doubled slash (no match).
- **The self-test does not cover either leak.** The seven new cases (`:422-456`) cover a nested package, a bare glob beside the path, the gate's own directory, a climbing path and a wildcard package. None covers a `.` segment or a partial match. The battery floor of 12 matches its 12 cases.

### ② Semver level
- **The changeset is right.** `.changeset/23974-package-doors-convert-forward.md` takes `minor` for `@objectstack/service-package` and `@objectstack/cloud-connection`. Doors 1 and 3 now admit bodies the registry used to refuse, and door 1 now hydrates the records after a refused one. No narrowing found: range-less bodies meet the identical judge, and door 3's readers move only toward current shapes.
- **`Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right with door 2 strict**, on both the PR body and the changeset. The claim spoke of three doors; it is now two, and that is still a widening. `Check Changeset` concluded success.
- **`@objectstack/metadata-protocol` needs no bump.** Its change is a comment only (13 added lines, all `//`, at `:31393-31405`), with no published behaviour change, so leaving it out of the changeset is right.
- The change is not breaking, so no ADR-0087 disposition marker is owed.

### ③ Boundary flags
- **`open_questions`:** empty; nothing to answer.
- **Flag 1** (class b, `checkProtocolCompat` refuses `^17.7.0 || ^18.0.0`): **confirmed by trace.** The union reaches the caret branch, which compares 18 with the union's first major. That breaks the handshake's own promise of never a false rejection (`protocol-handshake.ts:385-396`), on exactly the spelling an author would write to admit major 18. **ESCALATED to the seat:** no carrier appears in the inputs; file it.
- **Flag 2** (raw-ledger readers outside the claimed region): **the premise is wrong; the conclusion holds for two of the three readers.**
  - **The premise.** Conversions do rewrite translations, jobs and hooks today, each through a top-level `mapCollection` that reaches a flat package body (`packages/spec/src/conversions/registry.ts`). None rewrites seed `data`.
    - translations: `translation-validation-messages-removed`, `translation-per-app-settings-removed`, `translation-component-submit-label-removed`, `translation-widget-sub-caption-removed`;
    - jobs: `job-id-removed`, `job-timeout-to-timeout-ms`, `retry-policy-converged`;
    - hooks: `hook-timeout-to-timeout-ms`, `hook-body-crypto-hash-removed`.
  - **The `seedDatasetsOf(entry.manifest)` probes** (`:1875`, `:2670`) give no wrong answer: no conversion touches `data`.
  - **The install-time `unrunnableCode(ctx, manifest, …)`** (`:1428`) gives no wrong answer today. Its judges read a job's `enabled`, `pull`, `body`, `handler` and `name`, whether a hook has a `body`, and a mapping's `name` and `connectorSource` (`packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.ts:389-412`, `:457-491`, `:574-602`). No conversion touches any of these.
  - **The reseed `applySideEffects(ctx, entry.manifest, { … door: 'reseed' })`** (`:2542`) reads differently. It reloads the raw `translations` into i18n. So a per-app `settings` group from before 17.4 is loaded on reseed, while install and rehydrate (converted) load it stripped. `translation-per-app-settings-removed` strips that group because such an entry fills gaps in the merged served tree. Reach unmeasured.
  - **Disposition.** The reseed reader is outside the claimed region, so it is not a FAIL of this PR. But the acceptance note is false as written, and "Carrier: none" is wrong for that reader.
- **Flag 3** (`duplicatePackage`'s `catch {}`, `:27497-27499`): it predates this PR and is unchanged here. Agreed that it swallows a refusal silently. Escalated to the seat as a candidate card.
- **Flag 4** (the runtime's no-protocol fallback): agreed. It is the same authoring door, with D1 asserted at `:1408`.
